collision_mechanism_summary: In tables with repeated values (e.g. state 'CA', currency '0.00', status 'Active'), all rows produce identical text-level candidate matches. Hungarian alignment strictly pairs predicted rows to gold rows by value equality (identity assignment). Independent point-wise or greedy candidate selection picks whichever candidate has higher text/local score, causing multiple predicted rows to collide onto the same gold bbox, yielding 1 True Positive and N-1 False Positives.
